speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) what proportion of University students, Polytechnic and ITE students currently embark on work internships during their studies; (b) what is the duration and nature of these internships; and (c) what can be done to encourage more companies to provide internship opportunities for young Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: They provide students with meaningful learning experience in a real-world context, help them develop fuller perspectives of the various industries and better prepare them for work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Our post-Secondary education institutes (PSEIs) source and facilitate placements for students to go on internships.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Some students complete two or more internships during their studies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: In some instances, internships could last up to a year, depending on the structure of the courses that students are enrolled in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Internships are usually designed to complement the curriculum in the PSEIs, and to bridge theory and practice for the students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: The PSEIs work closely with industry partners to design internship programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: They identify key competencies that interns should acquire and other learning outcomes that would enhance the students’ employability in respective fields during internship.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: It is important to ensure that internships are carried out as intended and are meaningful for the students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: To this end, our PSEIs have been progressively enhancing the internships, such as introducing structured mentorships, to better meet our students’ learning needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Industry support is key in ensuring the availability and quality of internships for PSEI students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: The PSEIs frequently engage current and new industry partners, as well as companies, to explore new internship opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: They also tap on the help of industry associations and economic agencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Companies are increasingly willing to host interns to develop their talent pipeline and assess potential candidates for recruitment.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I just wanted to ask whether companies that offer internships to students consider the internship period as relevant work experience and whether they consider, in terms of employment thereafter, these students who have gone through the internship by giving them some increment in terms of salary, so that they get a higher salary grade when they are eventually employed by the companies.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank Dr Intan for her questions and I want to assure her that the PSEIs understand the value that the internship will bring to the students.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It will better prepare them for work, like she has shared, and the students also understand and appreciate the value that the internship will bring to their CV, really allowing them to have a better appreciation of what they have learnt in school, bridging theory and practice, so that they will be well placed to adjust to the workforce.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The example that Dr Intan has mentioned is aligned to why we started the SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme is a work-learn initiative that allows the graduates from polytechnic and ITE immediately upon their graduation, whether it is in ITE or polytechnic, to join a host company between 12 and 18 months, even longer.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is necessary for them to spend between 12 and 18 months because we are trying to achieve two objectives: to allow them to have meaningful work experience that is aligned to what they have learnt in polytechnic or ITE; at the same time, to build on that foundation such that they can even articulate to a specialist diploma if they were polytechnic graduates, or maybe a technical diploma if they graduate from ITE.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we do have a conduit to facilitate the intent that the Member has mentioned.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank Ms Sun Xueling for her two supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Even with the applied learning nature of the ITE education, actually, hands-on training is already very, very much part of the core curriculum of ITE now.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Member also asked about the Autonomous Universities (AUs).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to share that, as some AUs like the Singapore Management University, Singapore University of Technology and Design and Singapore University of Social Sciences, internships are already compulsory.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Singapore Institute of Technology has its eight- to 12-month long Integrated Work Study Programme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Internships are strongly encouraged at the National University of Singapore and Nanyang Technological University and in certain courses, attachments are a part of the curriculum such that for the undergraduates, they will have to complete internship as part of the graduation requirement.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: I would just like to seek a clarification on internship.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Do we really monitor the quality of internship programme?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: And do we evaluate it because companies may seem keen to provide internship but who does the monitoring, evaluation and feedback?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member Ms Thanaletchimi for the supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure her that the PSEIs take the quality of the internship very seriously.
